To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
P-cadherine is expressed by OSCC cells and that Slit-1 is a candidate tumour suppressive factor in OSCC cells.
Slit- 2 facilitates P-cadherins interaction with Robo- 3 and inhibits migration of oral squamous carcinoma cells.
Slit-1 and Slit-3 have no impact on P-cad-herin mediated cell migration, while Slit-2 inhibits P-cadherins mediated cell migration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of P-cad and Slit- 2 in OSCC.
the role of P-cad and Slit- 2 during OSCC development and progression.
the antitumorigenesis of Slit-1 in oral squamous cell carcinomas (OSCCs) and the underlying molecular mechanisms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Slit-1 and 2 are involved in the control of cell motility and migration in OSCC cells.
the expression of P-cad is associated with the expression of Slit-1 and Slit-3, and this is in turn associated with an inhibition of cell migration.
Slit-1, -2, and -3 are involved in the regulation of cell migration and cell adhesion in OSCC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
P-cadherins can function as tumour suppressors in OSCC via interaction with Slit-2/Robo- 3 signalling pathway.
P-cadherins can be used as a target to increase expression of Slit-1/2 in tumours, which in turn might inhibit cell migration and invasion of cancer cells.
Slit-3 is a candidate tumour suppressive factor for P-cadherine expressing OSCC cells and that Slit-1 and -2 can be regarded as potential biomarkers for P-cad expression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
P-cadherine expression in OSCC cells is a prerequisite for Slit-2 function.
P-cadherins and Slit-1/2/3 proteins are involved in the migration of OSCC cells and that this migration can be inhibited via Slit-2.
P-cadherins and Slits may have an important role in oral cancer progression and may serve as novel biomarkers and/or therapeutic targets.
